content: The task list exists so a requirement can be recorded mid-session without derailing the work in progress. That only holds if a queued task is never read as 'do this now'. So: memory_task_add's description says it queues and does not start; session start returns queued_tasks with services/task_brief.py, which tells the agent to surface the list and start nothing unless asked; enforcement.format_intro carries the count with the same framing; and the claim tool's description says to call it only when finished with what you were doing. The prompt-contract IS the feature - the storage is the easy part.
summary: The task list exists so a requirement can be recorded mid-session without derailing the work in progress
title: A queued task is a requirement, not an instruction

content:
Decided 2026-09-05 while rewriting the team the user asked for (dotnet, nodejs, react, app on top of the eight roles).

ONE BASE. agents/_base.md is abstract (never installed) and carries the contract every agent shares - Brain (session start, rules bind, search before deciding, store what outlives the task, project= on every write), Tasks (claim only when idle with your role; memory_task_start claims + clocks on + mirrors in_progress; comment as you go; attach evidence; stop the clock on every finish; memory_session_end last), Team (the dispatching session is the lead; cross-boundary changes are reported, not made), Discipline (tokens; never invent a tool, flag, endpoint or version; "not verified" over asserting; block on the user's decisions). The installer composes `extends:` chains (setup.compose_agent): a role's body lands at the base's {{EXTENSION}} marker, an expert's body at the role's, and the marker is stripped only at install. Rejected: eight files each restating the contract - that is exactly how the audit found eight files that said eight different things and none of which mentioned the clock.

EXPERTS EXTEND A ROLE, never the base directly: dotnet and nodejs extend backend (they inherit its craft, its worktree isolation and its hand-off to frontend), react and app extend frontend. Each expert's file is only its layer: the user's non-negotiables verbatim (NestJS/Next.js/pnpm; services as the business layer, lifecycle hooks, global + local exception filters; shadcn wrapped once and only the wrapper imported; Kotlin Multiplatform with Android and iOS pixel-identical and the platform-decided exceptions listed), a "currency without hallucination" rule (read the project's target versions first, name a feature with its version, mark the rest unverified), and what it produces when consulted before the implementing agent (a kind=decision task comment the backend/frontend agent implements from).

THE TEST GATE. Per the user's rule of 2026-09-05, the lead dispatches `test` to verify a change on the RUNNING product before committing it; test.md says so, the lead brief (enforcement.agent_team_intro) says so. The pytest suite (pre-commit hook) proves the code; the test agent proves the product.

SESSION IDS ARE EXPLICIT. Found on the first real dispatch: the desktop app's subagents share the parent's MCP connection, so the memory session the server remembers per connection is whichever session started last - the test agent's session start displaced the lead's and the lead's next memory_task_start claimed for the agent. Every agent therefore passes the session_id its own memory_session_start returned to memory_task_start, memory_task_claim_next and memory_session_end; the remembered session is only a convenience for a single session per connection. Rejected: refusing to overwrite an existing mapping - the agent's own task_start would then claim for the parent, the same bug mirrored.

COST. Composed bodies are 1.1-1.5k words (about 2k tokens) each, the roster line 300 chars, the session intro 3.5 KB. pm stays out of the dispatch roster; the main session is the lead.
entities: s body lands at the base
summary: Decided 2026-09-05 while rewriting the team the user asked for (dotnet, nodejs, react, app on top of the eight roles)
title: The agent team is composed from one base; experts extend a role; every agent passes its own session id

content: Several Claude sessions run against one project at once, and memory-mcp is one launchd daemon on 127.0.0.1:8765 that every session is an MCP client of - a second daemon cannot bind the port. So there is one writer and no fan-out to deduplicate. Work is never routed TO a session; a session asks FOR work when idle, which makes 'idle' definitionally correct with no heartbeat protocol. The claim is a conditional UPDATE (claimed_by IS NULL OR lease_expires_at < now) whose ROWCOUNT is the answer, serialized by a per-project threading.Lock in TaskService because DuckDB is single-writer and this repo opens a connection per operation. A plain lock is a COMPLETE fix for one daemon; if server mode ever runs several, the claim must move to the SQLite registry. Lease is 30 minutes, checked lazily on the next claim (no sweeper), renewed by any mutation of the task, and released by memory_session_end. Known limit: two machines means two daemons and two local rows that cannot see each other - cross-machine exclusion needs a server-side claim in asoode.
summary: Several Claude sessions run against one project at once, and memory-mcp is one launchd daemon on 127
title: Multi-session task claim: pull, don't push

content: SessionService.start loads active sprint items and recent decisions with limit=None (previously capped at 10 and 20). "Recent" is bounded by RECENT_DECISION_WINDOW (7 days), not by a count. Same rationale as MemoryRepository.get_rules, which has always been uncapped: a top-N sample silently drops context and nothing downstream can tell anything is missing. memory_search keeps its limit=10 default, because search is relevance-ranked by nature.
summary: Session context and rules load completely, never a top-N sample: SessionService
title: Session context and rules load completely, never a top-N sample

content:
Decided 2026-09-04 with the user, after two earlier mechanisms were tried and measured.

THE SHAPE: the session that talks to the user IS the technical lead. enforcement.agent_team_intro() injects the full orchestration brief at session start and agent_team_line() injects ONE line every turn, both through the UserPromptSubmit hook that already carries the binding rules. `pm` is excluded from the roster that brief advertises (enforcement.LEAD_AGENT), because dispatching pm re-creates the very layer this replaced. The pm.md file still exists and can be dispatched deliberately for a planning job worth doing in isolated context.

REJECTED: "the main session dispatches pm, and pm dispatches the specialists." The user proposed it; three measured objections decided against it.
- Subagent output is never shown to the user. Every layer is a lossy relay - the user saw pm's plan nearly verbatim today precisely because it was ONE hop.
- An orchestrating pm accumulates every agent's report, which is exactly the context cost pm's own fan-out rule exists to avoid. Its single planning dispatch cost 102,000 tokens.
- A running agent cannot be redirected, only the session can. The user interrupted twice during this very turn; both corrections would have been unreachable had pm been mid-chain.

ALSO REJECTED, and already retired: `agent: pm` in ~/.claude/settings.json, which setup used to write. Two faults. It is silently ignored by some clients - it was set on this machine and the desktop app started an ordinary session anyway, promising an orchestrator and delivering none. And alongside the hook it double-injects: a CLI session would get pm's prompt as its system prompt AND the brief every turn, with pm's tools and effort forced onto every unrelated one-off session. setup.retire_default_agent() removes it, and only ever the exact value the installer wrote - a hand-set agent is left alone.

THE PER-TURN LINE IS DELIBERATELY ONE LINE. It is injected on every prompt; a ninety-line orchestration prompt there is the token waste the team exists to avoid. The full roster and the economics go in the session-start intro only. A test asserts the per-turn line stays under 400 chars and single-line, and that a machine with no agents installed gets no injection at all.

RELATED, same session: skills are invoked rather than preloaded. `skills:` pulls a skill's full content into context at startup on EVERY dispatch, so designer names /design in its body and loads on demand; only reviewer preloads, because it uses code-review and security-review every run.
summary: Decided 2026-09-04 with the user, after two earlier mechanisms were tried and measured
title: The main session is the lead; the orchestration brief rides the hook

content: memory_import_rules copies rules with pending=True by default (schema v4 `pending` column). A pending memory is stored but inert: excluded from get_rules (the injected rule block), vector search, session context, the default listing, and the git snapshot. memory_session_start returns them as pending_adaptations with a brief (services/adaptation.py) telling the agent to rewrite each one for this codebase, dropping the source project's component names/paths/stack, and to ASK THE USER rather than guess. memory_adapt_pending(memory_id, title, content) clears the flag and puts the rule in force; memory_discard_pending drops it. metadata.imported_from keeps the original text and source project. Rationale: rules copied verbatim from another project read as authoritative and steer the agent wrong.
summary: memory_import_rules copies rules with pending=True by default (schema v4 `pending` column)
title: Rules imported from another project land pending and must be adapted first

content:
The bridge audit (docs/bridge/01, section 6) listed idempotency, assignee-on-create and a delta feed as hard blockers. Navid changed asoode instead: externalRef with @@unique on WorkPackage/WorkPackageList/WorkPackageTask (a repeated create returns the existing row), CreateTaskDto.description + assignees[]/assignSelf written in the same transaction, KartablDto.updatedSince/states/take/skip, and a socket handshake that accepts auth.token or a Bearer header.

This is why the outbound half needs no local mapping table: create-with-the-same-externalRef IS the lookup, so re-pushing is a no-op rather than a duplicate. Verified live - three pushes of 7 tasks left exactly 7 tasks on the board. One gap remains on the asoode side: work-packages.service.ts:149 maps board tasks through a private mapTask() that drops externalRef, so a board read cannot yet tell which local task a remote one came from.
summary: The bridge audit (docs/bridge/01, section 6) listed idempotency, assignee-on-create and a delta feed as hard blockers
title: The three Phase 2 blockers were fixed in asoode, not worked around here
